originalTitle: Polls begin closing in Michigan with eyes on high-stakes Democratic primary for US Senate seat – live updates
summary: Voters in Michigan are choosing between Abdul El-Sayed, a progressive former public health official, and representative Haley Stevens, a centrist backed by Democratic leaders, for a key US Senate seat
content: Ahead of polls closing, my colleague Joseph Gedeon has been speaking with voters in Detroit today. For David Sernick and Bonnie White, who live in Roseville Park, one race on the ballot mattered the most – the Democratic Senate primary. Sernick backed Abdul El-Sayed again, the same candidate he supported for governor in 2018. Sernick said he was drawn to a politician willing to be self-critical. “He’s comfortable criticizing ourselves as liberals, and we’ve got to do that,” Sernick said. White also backed El Sayed, but for a different reason. “I’m thinking about Israel and Palestine because that’s been a hot topic in the news recently,” she said. “I’ve been hearing a lot of noise around that.” Others noted that no matter who goes on to clinch the Democratic nomination, the party needs to band together and support them moving forward. “We’re really on the same team. How we go about it is the only difference,” said Roy Harris. For Mike Shane, a retired, self-described socialist stumping for Rashida Tlaib, this primary as a reckoning bigger than one Senate seat. He watched pro-Israel outsider groups, led by Aipac, blitz Haley Stevens’ campaign with $60 million in ad buys trying to beat El-Sayed, and he thinks the fight is only getting harder from here – including for rural conservatives losing hospitals, Medicaid, and food stamps. “This could be the Democratic Party’s Whig moment,” he mused, describing the party’s collapse and elimination in the 19th century. “We have similar questions right now with the rise of white supremacy, and we need to deal with it once and for all.” Polls have closed in Missouri, and we will be bringing you the results as they come through. We’ll be keeping an eye out on the Democratic primary in the state’s deep-blue first congressional district – where the pro-Israel incumbent, Wesley Bell, is facing a challenge from Cori Bush, a former progressive congresswoman who accuses Israel of perpetrating genocide in Gaza. Along with a heated Senate primary in Michigan, the Missouri contest has become a proxy battle over the Democratic party’s role in supporting Israel’s military before the November midterm elections. Almost all of the polls have closed in Michigan. We’ll bring you the results as they come in, particularly in the most closely watched race of the night – the Democratic primary for US Senate. There are four counties in Michigan that keep central time, which means that they will close their polls an hour later than the rest of the state. While Michigan’s Democratic Senate contest is the night’s marquee race, two House primaries also capture the fight over the party’s future. In the Great Lake state’s seventh congressional district – which flipped red in 2024 and is now held by Republican congressman Tom Barrett – a three-way race has emerged between progressive William Lawrence, a community organizer who co-founded the Sunrise Movement, Bridget Brink, the former US ambassador to Ukraine and former US Navy Seal Matt Maasdam. While the seat’s former representative, Senator Elissa Slotkin, has backed Massdam, independent Senator Bernie Sanders has endorsed Lawrence. Meanwhile, in the 13th district, which encompasses the Detroit area, Sanders also backed the state representative Donavan McKinney, another progressive running with the aim to oust the establishment-backed Democratic incumbent, representative Shri Thanedar. Joseph Gedeon reporting from Michigan: While outside a voting site in Dearborn, a confident Abdul El-Sayed not only believes he will win the primary, but has his sights set on Republican opponent Mike Rogers, predicting he “will beat [Rogers] by seven” in November. He called Rogers “generationally boring and generationally corrupt” adding that he “can’t decide what era of Republicanism he wants to be, so he carries the baggage of both.” “I’m hoping that that all of the senators who want to see a [Democratic] majority are going to team up, so we can all collectively dunk on Mike Rogers” he told reporters. Polls have closed in Virginia, where voters weighed in on primaries for all 11 US House seats and the Republican primary to pick a nominee to run against Democratic Senator Mark Warner. A reminder, Democrats are hoping to flip as many of the five GOP‑held House districts as possible this year – even after the state supreme court struck down their redistricting plan that would have netted them 10 of the 11 seats. Meanwhile, Republicans are also voting on a challenger in a long-shot effort take on Warner – a powerful Democrat who has served nearly 18 years in the Senate, and is running unopposed. This is also the incumbent’s final re-election bid, which Democrats are hoping will lift many of the down-ballot races going into November. Josh Young has watched the Democratic Party chase the center for years, and he’s done waiting. The 48-year-old small business owner cast his primary vote for Abdul El-Sayed, betting that progressive politics can finally break through. “We as Democrats have been putting out these centrist candidates for a long time with very little success,” he said. “I’m very hopeful that that tide is shifting.” By Rachel Leingang and Joseph Gedeon The Israel-Gaza war created gaping divisions in the Democratic party and contributed to a resounding loss in a critical presidential election year in 2024. Two years later, the issue continues to dominate races across the country, as progressives try to seize on Israel’s falling popularity and a broad anti-war sentiment ahead of November’s midterms. chineseTitle: 密歇根州的民意调查开始结束，关注美国参议院席位的高风险民主党初选——实时更新
chineseSummary: 密歇根州的选民正在进步派前公共卫生官员阿卜杜勒·赛义德和民主党领导人支持的中间派众议员海莉·史蒂文斯之间进行选择，争夺美国参议院的一个重要席位
chineseContent: 在投票结束之前，我的同事约瑟夫·吉登今天一直在底特律与选民交谈。对于住在罗斯维尔公园的大卫·瑟尼克和邦妮·怀特来说，选票上的一场比赛最重要——民主党参议院初选。瑟尼克再次支持阿卜杜勒·赛义德，即他在 2018 年支持的州长候选人。瑟尼克表示，他被一位愿意自我批评的政客所吸引。 “他很乐意批评我们作为自由主义者，我们必须这样做，”瑟尼克说。怀特也支持埃尔·赛义德，但出于不同的原因。 “我正在考虑以色列和巴勒斯坦，因为这是最近新闻中的热门话题，”她说。 “我听到周围有很多噪音。”其他人指出，无论谁最终获得民主党提名，该党都需要团结起来并支持他们前进。 “我们真的是在同一个团队。我们的处理方式是唯一的区别，”罗伊·哈里斯说。对于迈克·谢恩（Mike Shane）来说，这位退休的、自称是拉希达·特莱布（Rashida Tlaib）竞选对手的社会主义者，对他来说，这次初选比一个参议院席位更重要。他看到以 Aipac 为首的亲以色列的局外人团体斥资 6000 万美元的广告购买闪电战海莉·史蒂文斯 (Haley Stevens) 的竞选活动，试图击败埃尔·赛义德 (El-Sayed)，他认为战斗从这里开始只会变得更加艰难 — — 包括让农村保守派失去医院、医疗补助和食品券。 “这可能是民主党的辉格党时刻，”他沉思道，描述了该党在 19 世纪的崩溃和消灭。 “随着白人至上主义的兴起，我们现在也面临着类似的问题，我们需要一劳永逸地解决这个问题。”密苏里州的投票已经结束，我们将在结果公布后为您带来结果。我们将密切关注该州深蓝色第一国会选区的民主党初选
